handbookNote: Source: Nebraska Class O Driver's Manual (Nebraska DMV, English edition 1-2025), fetched directly as a PDF from dmv.nebraska.gov (https://dmv.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/Class%20O%20Drivers%20Manual-English%201-2025.pdf) and extracted to text with pdftotext -- full compiled text saved to temp/handbooks/ne/raw_driver_manual_extracted.txt. Price matches this project's established Driver tier ($4.99), not a placeholder. Exam mechanics: real, documented effort was made to confirm the official item count, passing score, and time limit for Nebraska's Class O knowledge test from dmv.nebraska.gov (manual itself, FAQ-style pages, learner's permit/operator's license pages, online practice test tool) plus Nebraska Revised Statutes Chapter 60 (examination-related sections) -- none of these official sources publish a specific question count, pass percentage, or time limit; the manual only states that 'over 32% of first-time applicants fail the written test' and that its own back-of-manual practice exam (39 sample items, T/F plus multiple choice, provided by AAA Nebraska/Cornhusker Motor Club Foundation) uses DIFFERENT questions than the real test and is explicitly NOT a stand-in for the actual item count or passing threshold. These specific numbers are therefore UNCONFIRMED from any official source found -- not invented or defaulted. Content-depth rationale: the manual's substantive driving-rules content (Sections 1-7, roughly pages 1-73) is unusually rich and numerically specific -- exact ages/timelines for every permit type and GDL stage, a full point-value table, precise BAC-impairment breakpoints, exact speed limits by road type, exact distances/fines for parking, passing, move-over, railroad crossings, and child-restraint/insurance/equipment thresholds -- which comfortably supports a 250+ question pool of distinct, non-repetitive, directly grounded questions without padding.
